risks.title: Antitrust and Regulatory Actions
risks.score_rationale: Alphabet faces adverse rulings in the U.S. DOJ Search and Ad Tech antitrust cases, EC DMA designation, UK CMA scrutiny and similar global actions. Potential remedies include divestitures and behavioural restrictions on default search and ad tech.
risks.summary: Ongoing antitrust cases globally could force structural remedies including divestitures, behavioural changes to default search agreements and limits on Google's ad tech stack.

risks.title: AI Competition and Search Disruption
risks.score_rationale: Generative AI from OpenAI, Microsoft, Anthropic and Meta threatens Google's core search query monetization. Alphabet has materially increased capex for AI infrastructure with uncertain ROI.
risks.summary: Competition from generative AI assistants and chatbots could erode Google Search query volume and CPCs, while AI capex compresses near-term margins.

risks.title: Advertising Revenue Concentration
risks.score_rationale: Advertising remains the dominant revenue source (Search, YouTube, Network). Cyclical ad spend and ATT-style privacy changes directly impact growth.
risks.summary: Cyclical advertising demand, privacy regulation and platform-level changes to identifiers could compress ad pricing and volume.

risks.title: Privacy Regulation and Data Protection
risks.score_rationale: GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, EU AI Act, India DPDPA and similar regimes impose fines and constrain data use. Multiple ongoing EU and U.S. state privacy investigations.
risks.summary: Evolving global privacy and AI regulations could increase compliance costs, restrict targeted advertising and result in material fines.

risks.title: Capital Intensity and AI Infrastructure ROI
risks.score_rationale: Capex has roughly doubled to fund TPUs, GPUs and data centers for AI. Returns are uncertain and depreciation will increasingly pressure operating margin.
risks.summary: Surging AI-related capex could compress free cash flow and margins if monetization of AI services lags infrastructure investment.

risks.title: Content, Safety and AI Liability
risks.score_rationale: YouTube and Generative AI outputs expose Alphabet to defamation, IP infringement, child safety and misinformation litigation. Section 230 reform debates add uncertainty.
risks.summary: Litigation and regulation over user-generated content, AI hallucinations and IP infringement could result in material liability and content moderation costs.

risks.title: Geopolitical and Trade Risk
risks.score_rationale: Operations and revenues exposed to U.S.-China tensions, export controls on AI chips, Russia exit and content moderation conflicts with foreign governments.
risks.summary: Trade restrictions, sanctions and content-related disputes with foreign governments could disrupt operations and access to AI hardware.
